description:

Business owners: Want to scale faster? We provide in-person advisory for companies doing at least $1M per year: https://www.acquisition.com/workshop-yth

If you’re new to my channel, my name is Alex Hormozi. I’m the founder and managing partner of Acquisition.com. It’s a family office, which is just a formal way of saying we invest our own money into companies. Our 10 portfolio companies bring in over $250,000,000+ per year. Our ownership stake varies between 20% and 100% of them. Given this is a YT channel, and anyone can claim anything, I’ll give you some stuff you can google to verify below.

How I got here…

21: Graduated Vanderbilt in 3 years Magna Cum Laude, and took a fancy consulting job.
23 yrs old: Left my fancy consulting job to start a business (a gym).
24 yrs old: Opened 5 gym locations.
26 yrs old: Closed down 6th gym. Lost everything. 
26 yrs old: Got back to launching gyms (launched 33). Then, lost everything for a 2nd time. 
26 yrs old: In desperation, started licensing model as a hail mary. It worked. 
27 yrs old: "Gym Launch" does $3M profit the next 6 months. Then $17M profit next 12 months.
28 yrs old: Started Prestige Labs. $20M the first year.  
29 yrs old: Launched ALAN, a software company for agencies to work leads for customers. Scaled to $1.7mmo within 6 months. 
31 yrs old: Sold 75% of UseAlan to a strategic buyer in an all stock deal. 
31 yrs old: Sold 66% of Gym Launch & Prestige Labs at $46.2M valuation in all-cash deal to American Pacific Group. (you can google it)
31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses. 
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com to help the many people who want to start a business online do so.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

To all the gladiators in the arena, we’re all in the middle of writing our own stories. The worse the monsters, the more epic the story.

You either get an epic outcome or an epic story. Both mean you win. 

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles. 

Never quit,

Alex

If you’re new to my channel, my name is Alex Hormozi. I’m the founder and managing partner of Acquisition.com. It’s a family office, which is just a formal way of saying we invest our own money into companies. Our 10 portfolio companies bring in over $250,000,000+ per year. Our ownership stake varies between 20% and 100% of them. Given this is a YT channel, and anyone can claim anything, I’ll give you some stuff you can google to verify below.

How I got here…

21: Graduated Vanderbilt in 3 years Magna Cum Laude, and took a fancy consulting job.
23 yrs old: Left my fancy consulting job to start a business (a gym).
24 yrs old: Opened 5 gym locations.
26 yrs old: Closed down 6th gym. Lost everything. 
26 yrs old: Got back to launching gyms (launched 33). Then, lost everything for a 2nd time. 
26 yrs old: In desperation, started licensing model as a hail mary. It worked. 
27 yrs old: "Gym Launch" does $3M profit the next 6 months. Then $17M profit next 12 months.
28 yrs old: Started Prestige Labs. $20M the first year.  
29 yrs old: Launched ALAN, a software company for agencies to work leads for customers. Scaled to $1.7mmo within 6 months. 
31 yrs old: Sold 75% of UseAlan to a strategic buyer in an all stock deal. 
31 yrs old: Sold 66% of Gym Launch & Prestige Labs at $46.2M valuation in all-cash deal to American Pacific Group. (you can google it)
31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses. 
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com to help the many people who want to start a business online do so.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

You either get an epic outcome or an epic story. Both mean you win. 

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles. 

Never quit,

Alex

description:
Everybody is chasing the exact same shiny business models right now. Drop-shipping, building a software company, creating a flashy direct-to-consumer clothing brand. But when you actually open the books on those companies, the reality is often brutal. After you pay for manufacturing, international shipping, warehouse storage, Facebook ads, customer service software, and a team of developers, a successful e-commerce or software brand is lucky to walk away with a 15 to 20 percent net profit margin. You could be making a million dollars a year in revenue and only taking home a small fraction of that, all while working eighty-hour weeks and dealing with massive operational headaches.

The smartest money is hiding in plain sight. It is sitting in boring, ugly, unsexy businesses that nobody talks about at parties. These are operations with almost zero overhead, no inventory, no massive teams, and profit margins that consistently hover around 90 percent. When your expenses are just a laptop, an internet connection, and your own specialized knowledge, nearly every dollar that comes through the door stays in your bank account.

Here are five unsexy businesses with 90 percent profit margins that you can start right now.

title: 13 "Poor Man's Side Hustles" That Still Pay $1,000 a Week in 2026
description:
In nineteen ninety-one a man in Dayton, Ohio lost a warehouse job he had held for eleven years, and spent six hundred of his last nine hundred dollars on four used vending machines. His first week they took in sixty-one dollars and he nearly gave up. He now runs forty-one machines across a county and has not had a boss in thirty-four years.

That is the pattern behind every one of these thirteen. The side hustles that actually reach a thousand dollars a week are almost never the exciting ones. They are the quiet, slightly unglamorous jobs that already existed in your grandfather's town under an older name — the delivery boy, the washerwoman, the scavenger, the travelling sharpener, the odd-job man, the auctioneer, the teamster. The tools changed and the language changed. The work did not.

None of this is about apps, and none of it can be started from a phone in your bed. Every one of these needs you to leave the house and be reliable, and that is the entire barrier — which is exactly why the field is thinner than you would expect. A thousand dollars a week is the bar on all thirteen, roughly fifty-two thousand a year, and the arithmetic is shown on each one.

Watch what they share at the end, because it is the only part that really transfers. Not one of them got to a thousand a week by working harder than the people who quit. They got there by turning jobs into a route — the same customers, the same day, every week, until finding work stopped being part of the job.

These are 13 "Poor Man's Side Hustles" that still pay $1,000 a week in 2026. Number six runs on a fixed route your great-grandfather would recognise, and number one is the only one on the list that pays you while you are asleep.

Which of these would you actually be willing to do? Tell me in the comments — and if you have run one, what week did it finally start working?

title: How to go ALL IN on your side hustle...
description:
Get your free personalized $100M scaling roadmap: https://www.acquisition.com/roadmap

If you’re new to my channel, my name is Alex Hormozi. I’m the founder and managing partner of Acquisition.com. It’s a family office, which is just a formal way of saying we invest our own money into companies. Our 10 portfolio companies bring in over $250,000,000+ per year. Our ownership stake varies between 20% and 100% of them. Given this is a YT channel, and anyone can claim anything, I’ll give you some stuff you can google to verify below.

How I got here…

21: Graduated Vanderbilt in 3 years Magna Cum Laude, and took a fancy consulting job.
23 yrs old: Left my fancy consulting job to start a business (a gym).
24 yrs old: Opened 5 gym locations.
26 yrs old: Closed down 6th gym. Lost everything. 
26 yrs old: Got back to launching gyms (launched 33). Then, lost everything for a 2nd time. 
26 yrs old: In desperation, started licensing model as a hail mary. It worked. 
27 yrs old: "Gym Launch" does $3M profit the next 6 months. Then $17M profit next 12 months.
28 yrs old: Started Prestige Labs. $20M the first year.  
29 yrs old: Launched ALAN, a software company for agencies to work leads for customers. Scaled to $1.7mmo within 6 months. 
31 yrs old: Sold 75% of UseAlan to a strategic buyer in an all stock deal. 
31 yrs old: Sold 66% of Gym Launch & Prestige Labs at $46.2M valuation in all-cash deal to American Pacific Group. (you can google it)
31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses. 
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com, which is a platform for people to build communities online, making a living doing what they love, with people like them.
36 yrs old: I did a $106M book launch selling 3.6M copies of my $100M Money Models book, in 72 hours, breaking the Guinness world record for the fastest selling non-fiction book of all time.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

To all the gladiators in the arena, we’re all in the middle of writing our own stories. The worse the monsters, the more epic the story.

You either get an epic outcome or an epic story. Both mean you win. 

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles. 

Never quit,

Alex

title: 15 Boring Businesses That Make Money While You Sleep (Recurring Revenue)
description:
In 15 BORING BUSINESSES That Make Money While You Sleep, we break down 15 ordinary businesses that can generate recurring revenue and become less dependent on the owner's time as systems, employees, technology, and repeat customers are put in place.

From commercial cleaning and vending machines to self-storage, laundromats, equipment rental, bookkeeping, portable restroom rentals, and buying an existing business — these are businesses built around problems people repeatedly need solved.

description:
What if your business could keep making money while you sleep?

Most people think making more money means working more hours.

But what if the smarter move was to build something once, create a system around it, and let that system keep generating revenue after you're done working?

In this video, we're breaking down 10 businesses that are built around automation, digital assets, recurring revenue, rentals, and convenience.

Some can require serious upfront investment. Others can be started with relatively little money.

But there's one psychological pattern connecting all of them:

People don't always pay for the thing itself.

They pay to save time.
They pay for convenience.
They pay for an experience.
They pay to avoid doing something themselves.

And once you understand that, ordinary problems can start looking like business opportunities.

I'll also show you why some of these seemingly boring businesses can become surprisingly powerful when you combine automation with repeat customers and assets that can be used again and again.
